shorts.title: What you will learn: Static members
shorts.hook: One value, shared by every object.
shorts.script: One value, shared by every object. Today we share data between objects. A static member belongs to the class, and every object sees the same one. A normal member belongs to each object. A static member belongs to the class. There is only one copy, and every object shares it. Since C plus plus seventeen, you can write inline static and set the value inside the class. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Static members.

shorts.title: Static members in one minute
shorts.hook: A normal member belongs to each object.
shorts.script: A normal member belongs to each object. A static member belongs to the class. There is only one copy, and every object shares it. Since C plus plus seventeen, you can write inline static and set the value inside the class. A static function has no this pointer, so it can only use static members. Think of a school notice board. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: A static function belongs to the class.
shorts.script: A static function belongs to the class. We can call it without an object. We write the class name, two colons, and the function name. One hundred degrees Celsius is two hundred twelve degrees Fahrenheit. The program prints two hundred twelve. A static member belongs to the class. All objects share one copy. Reach it with the class name and two colons. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A static function that uses a normal member
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in static members?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in static members? Bug of the Day. A static function tries to read a normal member. The compiler says invalid use of member in static member function. A static function has no object, so it has no count. Make the function normal, and call it on an object. A normal member belongs to an object. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A static function that uses a normal member.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you count the objects in static members?
shorts.script: Can you count the objects in static members? Why is the static member so popular? Everybody shares it, and nobody pays rent. Write a class with a static counter. Count how many objects exist. Print the count after you make five. Write your answer in the comments. A static member belongs to the class. All objects share one copy. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
